sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 12.05.2023 passed in MACC.No.438 of 2021 by 5th M.A.C.T.,
Mandla District- Mandla seeking setting aside of impugned award and grant of suitable compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the instant case, accident occurred on 19.07.2021 and on 22.07.2021, deceased Deep Singh's name came to be recorded in RTO records.
Thus, on the date of accident, respondent No.1 Awadesh was registered owner of offending vehicle and deceased Deep Singh was not registered owner.

In the instant case, accident has occurred on account of rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by Ajay Maravi, on account of which, offending vehicle slipped and thereby Ajay Maravi and Deep Singh, who was sitting as pillion rider, both sustained injuries and succumbed to the same.
Learned counsel for the appellant has also referred to Section 2(30) of Motor Vehicle Act and relevant paras of impugned award.

With respect of above submissions, learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar and Others reported in 2018 (3) SCC 1.
4.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar and Others reported in 2018 (3) SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has submitted that findings recorded by the Tribunal are just and proper and no interference is required.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.
6. Primary issue involved in the case is whether on the date of accident, deceased was owner of offending vehicle or not.
In the instant case, accident has occurred on 19.07.2021 and deceased's name came to be recorded in RTO records on 22.07.2021.

But perusal of documents Ex.D/1 to D/6 reveal that registered owner Awadesh/respondent No.1 had sold offending vehicle to deceased Deep Singh on 01.06.2021 and had also delivered possession thereof to Deep Singh.
Thus, on the date of accident, offending vehicle was in possession of deceased Deep Singh and he was owner of the same.

7. In Naveen Kumar (Supra) Hon'ble Apex Court has held that in view of definition of the expression "owner" in Section 2(30) of the MV Act, 1988, it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered who, for the purposes of the said Act, would be treated as the "owner".

But in this Court's opinion, from above, it cannot be inferred and neither it establishes so that a person who had purchased vehicle from registered owner and has also received possession but his name is yet to be recorded in RTO records and any accident occurs in between purchase's of motor vehicle and transfer of purchaser's name in RTO records as owner, such owner can still claim compensation from person who is registered as owner in RTO records 8.

Present claim petition has been filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act against Awadesh,
registered owner of offending vehicle and Insurance Company of offending vehicle.
Present claim petition has been filed by claimants, who are parents of owner of offending vehicle.

9. In the instant case, Insurance policy of offending vehicle (Ex.D/7) is also on record and it is evident from the same that it is "Liability only policy" and not "comprehensive/package policy".
Ganga Bai vs Awdesh Jhariya on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60474422/
2 10.
Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, appellants are not entitled to receive any compensation from respondents.
10. In the light of above, I have gone through the findings recorded by the Tribunal, in this Court's opinion, no ground is made out for interference in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
In the instant case, principle laid down in Naveen Kumar (Supra) does not help the appellant in any way.
11. Hence, in view of discussion in the foregoing paras, appeal filed by appellant is dismissed and findings recorded by the Tribunal are affirmed.
12. Appeal filed by appellants is disposed off accordingly.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Ganga Bai vs Awdesh Jhariya on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60474422/
